body:
First-touch grading (triage seat): promoted to `pm:queue`, type Bug. The published zod validator rejects spellings the published TS declaration and the live renderer both accept — declared≠enforced on a published surface. The widening itself was already ruled in #4581 for the TS side; aligning the mirror inherits that ruling rather than opening a new contract question. Executor constraints from the card: `visible`/`disabled` → `z.union([z.boolean(), z.string()])`; `ariaLabel` → the **KeyedI18nLabel** object shape, NOT the spec's inline locale map — read #4580's Q2-B ruling (comment 5284007579) before writing it. The larger "derive or parity-test the mirror so it cannot drift again" question may be included if cheap, or filed separately. Size: M, `mode:subagent`.

```json
  "summary": "The premise held and the census GREW: the mirror had drifted narrower on FIVE keys, not three. label/description also widened to `string | I18nLabel` under #4580's revised Q1-A ruling — whose acceptance comment (5285975071) recorded exactly this: '#4605's census grows by label/description as noted.' Shapes as ruled: visible/disabled -> z.union([z.boolean(), z.string()]); ariaLabel -> the KEYED object via a new exported KeyedI18nLabelSchema (NOT the spec's inline locale map, per #4580 Q2-B); label/description -> the spec's own I18nLabelSchema embedded BY REFERENCE. The two i18n vocabularies are kept apart rather than merged into 'some object' — merging would have reproduced #4167's confusability hazard inside the validator meant to catch it — and both cross pairings are pinned as rejections. label/description were taken in-place under the bounded exemption (same defect class, same file, same gate family, no other claim on the path, shape pinned by the TS declaration plus the spec's own schema); the decisive reason is that the anti-drift pin CANNOT be written without them, since it asserts the drift set is empty and stays red while any of the five is narrow. The card's larger question (derive-or-parity-test) is INCLUDED rather than filed, because it measured cheap: the pin reads the mirror's own .shape and compares each key to the declaration, so the next widening that forgets this file turns red with no key list to maintain. Nothing narrowed; every spelling that parsed before still parses.",
  "tests": "All at final commit 85c441174 (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), re-run AFTER the last commit. RED-FIRST (unmodified mirror, 10 cases, predictions written first, 0 mismatches): visible '${data.status === \"open\"}' -> `expected boolean, received string`; disabled likewise; ariaLabel {key,defaultValue} -> `expected string, received object`; label {en,'zh-CN'} and description {en} -> same. Five already-valid controls accepted. GREEN: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` exit 0 (script name echoed, so no zero-match --filter); `vitest run packages/types` -> 'Test Files 43 passed (43) / Tests 490 passed (490)'; `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` exit 0 (all three tsc projects); `turbo type-check` over the six DOWNSTREAM consumers of @object-ui/types/zod (cli, fields, plugin-list, plugin-map, plugin-view, runner) -> 'Tasks: 24 successful, 24 total', each of the six :type-check tasks confirmed present in the output; gates check:control-bytes, check:esm-specifiers, check:phantom-deps, check:self-import, check:spec-symbols, check:i18n-keys all exit 0. Exit codes captured by redirect-then-capture, never after a pipe. ABLATION — 5 legs, each direction predicted before running, all 5 matched. NO REBUILD LEG WAS NEEDED, and that is MEASURED not assumed: the test imports '../zod/base.zod.js' relatively and vitest aliases @object-ui/types -> packages/types/src, so resolution is to SOURCE; the proof is that dist/ still held the PRE-FIX build (`visible: z.boolean().optional()`) at the moment the widened tests passed, so nothing under test resolves through dist/. Mutations confirmed on disk by occurrence count (`grep -o | wc -l`, injected AND deleted text, never a bare diffstat); restored under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`; restore verified BY SHA256 (82c8f7d4... / f10e815b..., both matched pristine). L1 visible->z.boolean(): predicted parity pin RED + 1 test RED; observed TS2344 line 94, '1 failed | 12 passed'. L2 ariaLabel->z.string(): predicted pin RED + 1 test RED with the cross-rejection staying GREEN (a bare string schema also refuses objects); observed exactly that. L3 ariaLabel->the withdrawn I18nLabel spelling: predicted pin RED + 2 tests RED; observed TS2344 line 94, '2 failed | 11 passed' — this is the defect the card exists to prevent. L4 MirroredKeys->never: predicted guard RED with the MAIN PIN VACUOUSLY GREEN; observed TS2344 at line 106 ONLY (line 94 silent), runtime 13 passed — the load-bearing leg. L5 MirroredKeys->string: predicted literal-guard RED; observed TS2536 line 79 + TS2344 line 123, runtime 13 passed. Line 94=assertionMirrorIsNotNarrower, 106=assertionShapeKeysResolve, 123=assertionShapeKeysAreLiteral. ONE VOID LEG, reported not silently retried: the first ablation attempt returned 'VERDICT queue-timeout (exit 99) - never acquired' after 540s on the shared verify lock, so the wrapped script never executed and no mutation was applied (tree confirmed unchanged); the legs were rerun batched into a single acquisition. DECLARED NARROWING: eslint run over the 2 changed source files, not repo-wide — 2 files linted per --format json, 0 errors, 1 warning, and that warning is PRE-EXISTING (the `any` type argument on SchemaNodeSchema's z.ZodType annotation, verbatim at origin/main line 24, untouched by this diff, shifted to line 51 by the insertion above it). The narrowing excludes nothing: no type-aware linting is configured (no project/projectService in the eslint config), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide scan is CI's run. CI convergence is PM's per the standing contract; gates were in_progress at report time.",
  "open_questions": [],
  "out_of_scope_findings": [
    "NOT FILED — GitHub search API returned 'rate limit already exceeded' when I went to dedupe-search, and filing discipline is search-before-file (parallel devs cannot see each other's same-hour cards). Handing it to PM rather than risking a duplicate or dropping it: the derived parity construction added here guards BaseSchema ONLY; the ~17 sibling mirrors in packages/types/src/zod/ (form, views, crud, app, blocks, ...) mirror their own TS types with no equivalent guard, and that defect class has now produced at least two confirmed instances (this card, and #5186 for FormFieldSchema.validation). Observation-class: `finding` label, no `pm:queue`. The construction is ~10 lines and transplantable per mirror."
  ]
}
```
